bugs_found: loan_payment uses generic Exception instead of ValueError for negative principal, breaking consistent error handling and except ValueError callers
compound_interest performs r/n with Decimal division which loses precision when n does not divide r exactly; should use higher precision context or rearrange formula
transfer is not atomic: if a later operation fails between the two balance assignments, funds can be lost (no try/except rollback or transactional wrapper)
transfer compares accounts by identity (is) instead of by id, so two Account objects representing the same account would not be detected as self-transfer
apply_fee treats fee_pct as a raw multiplier (e.g. 0.02) without documenting it; passing a percentage like 2 would charge 200% fee with no sanity cap
fx_convert does not validate that the rate is positive; a zero or negative rate in the dict would silently produce wrong results
fx_convert lacks reverse-rate fallback: if only (USD,EUR) is provided, converting EUR->USD raises instead of using 1/rate
loan_payment zero-rate branch returns p/m without rounding to currency precision (sub-cent fractions leak)
compound_interest accepts years as int(years) silently truncating floats (e.g. 2.5 years becomes 2), which is surprising for a finance API
No monetary quantization/rounding to 2 decimal places anywhere; returned Decimals can have many digits, leading to inconsistent downstream rounding
Account.balance and amount are not validated to be Decimal in transfer; passing float amount mixes types and can raise TypeError or lose precision
Receipt has no timestamp, currency, or transaction id, making it insufficient as an audit record for financial transfers
No logging/audit trail for transfer or fee application, which is a compliance concern for financial code
apply_fee silently returns a negative-ish result is prevented but does not check that fee_max is reasonable vs amount; result can be zero with no warning
Type hints missing on all public functions, hurting maintainability and static analysis
